events.title: Hubble gets corrective optics
events.description: Astronauts service the space telescope to improve its images.

events.title: South Africa holds a democratic election
events.description: The country holds its first national democratic election open to all races.

events.title: Windows 95 reaches stores
events.description: Microsoft launches a new operating system with a Start menu and taskbar.

what_happened_next.text:
Disney more than doubled, leading this set. The US share basket roughly doubled, and IBM nearly did. Wal-Mart lost about one-fifth of its value. The world’s political map changed, yet companies still followed different paths. Even a successful retailer could disappoint someone buying its stock at this starting date.

During the period, astronauts fitted corrective equipment to Hubble in 1993. South Africa held its first national democratic election open to all races in 1994. Windows 95 reached shops in 1995, changing the experience of using many home computers.

These events help put the years in order. They do not prove why a particular stock rose or fell. A new product, an election and a scientific success can matter greatly without giving you a simple investing instruction.

The starting headlines included job cuts and hopes for recovery. An investor had to decide with that mixed picture. The completed chart supplies information that was missing then: the timing, size and order of the gains and losses.

reflection.what_people_were_focused_on: The Soviet Union had ended, South Africa was negotiating change, and the US economy needed support. Job cuts and holiday products appeared side by side.
reflection.what_actually_mattered: Company share prices did not all follow the broad market. Owning many businesses reduced reliance on the fortunes of one retailer or entertainment company.
reflection.what_faded_away: The popularity of a particular holiday product did not predict an entire company’s five-year return. A rate cut was also only one part of the picture.
reflection.what_nobody_knew: No one could know the exact investment ranking. New political institutions and new products would take years to develop.

hot_stock_outcomes.text: The Lion King became a major success in 1994, giving Disney another valuable set of characters. Disney also completed the ABC purchase in February 1996. Meanwhile, its Paris park needed a new financing deal to manage its debts in 1994 after opening in 1992. The strong investment gain covered both successful entertainment and a project that needed financial repair.

IBM’s recovery produced about $3 billion of profit in 1994 and $4.2 billion in 1995. Buying Lotus in 1995 added software, while growing services helped customers run their computer systems. The investment rose strongly as earnings recovered from the company’s earlier losses and its business became less dependent on selling machines alone.

Walmart kept growing: sales reached about $94 billion in the year ending January 1996, up 13%, and its US supercenters reached 239. Yet profit grew only about 2% that year. The investment finished lower. More stores and higher sales did not automatically mean equally fast profit growth or a good return from this starting price.
